new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress falls on the penultimate syllable of the word (counting prefixes: a monosyllabic root with a prefix is stressed on the prefix). A closed set of final suffixes — absolutive -tli, locative -co, plural -ten, agentive -qui — is extrametrical, so words ending in them are stressed on the antepenult (i.e., on the penult of the base). Spanish loans are re-stressed to the penult. Elsewhere in the same ms. (p. 18-19) the author uses the rule that 'the stress is always on the penultimate syllable in Nahuatl' to decide vowel-length/syllabification questions.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned. (p. 21: a reduplicated vowel sequence is 'audibly two syllable nucleuses, receiving two stresses', versus one long vowel.)
new_statements.exceptions: Final -tli, -co, -ten, -qui not counted (stress on antepenult); prefix stressed when root is monosyllabic; Spanish loans shifted to penultimate stress (doctor, café, corral, fiscal, reloj). Hedged with 'usually'.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (phonological word including prefixes), citation forms in phonetic transcription; draft manuscript 'posted as is without peer review'. The variety described is that of San Miguel Tenango (municipio de Zacatlán), which SIL/ISO treat as the reference lect of nhi.
new_statements.identity_note: The statement source describes the Nahuatl of San Miguel Tenango, municipio de Zacatlán, Puebla ('SMT Nahuatl'), which SIL and ISO 639-3 treat as the reference lect of nhi (Ethnologue alternate name 'Tenango Nahuatl'; Glottolog zaca1241, no child languoids). It does not cover the Ahuacatlán or Tepetzintla villages directly. Glottolog's ref 547285 'Bartholomew, Doris (n.d.), Gramática del Náhuatl de San Miguel Tenango' is the same SIL manuscript now catalogued as Schroeder 2014 (the 'Bartholomew Collection' is the archive series name, not the author). Brockway 1963/1979 'North Puebla Nahuatl' (Naupan) belongs to Northern Puebla Nahuatl [ncj] (Glottolog nort2957), not to this language.
